synthesis: DEV-2468 replaces the zero-query `UniqueScansLeaderboard` stub (already registered at its exact mockup slot, row 3 col 1, by the DEV-2409 stub PR) with a real per-kit unique-plate leaderboard for the Company Metrics dashboard. The underlying ClickHouse cost question the ticket worried about is already retired: DEV-2466's spike proved `GROUP BY kit_id WITH ROLLUP` on `clarity.scans_cold` (org_id-filtered, no FINAL) answers both DEV-2467's org total (the `kit_id=0` rollup row) and this card's per-kit ranking from one scan, and DEV-2467 already shipped that exact query (`ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery::handleRange()`) plus a class-neutral cache key (`sharedRangeCacheKey()`) built specifically so this card can read it instead of issuing a second scan. The genuine remaining work is narrower than the ticket implies: (1) swap the stub's base class from `DashboardWidget` to the ChartWidget-direct `DashboardMetricCard` shape `RecoveryLeader`/`StagingLiveHitLeader` use (a scalar-per-month model cannot hold a per-kit ranking), (2) wire the compact stat to the already-shared current-window rollup for the headline and to `UniqueScanCounts`'s already-cached monthly org-total series for the sparkline (both zero-marginal-cost reads, not new queries), and (3) resolve one real design fork the ticket does not settle: whether the expanded detail view needs a genuine 13-month x per-kit breakdown, which `ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery::handle()` deliberately does not provide and DEV-2466 never measured, or whether a leaderboard's expanded view is just the current-window ranked list plus the same org-total sparkline the compact card shows.

scope.summary: Rewrite `UniqueScansLeaderboard` in place to extend `ChartWidget` + `implements DashboardMetricCard` (the RecoveryLeader/StagingLiveHitLeader shape) instead of `DashboardWidget`, gate it on `FeatureEnum::COMPANY_METRICS` (matching UniqueScanCounts/StagingLiveHitLeader), source its headline + per-kit ranking from the already-shared `ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery::handleRange()` rollup via `sharedRangeCacheKey()` (zero new ClickHouse calls when UniqueScanCounts, which renders first, has already populated it for the same org/window/tz), and source its 13-point sparkline from `UniqueScanCounts`'s already-cached monthly org-total buckets rather than any new query. Remove the now-dead `'unique-scans-leaderboard'` arm from `DashboardWidget::getStatColor()` since a ChartWidget-direct card never calls that method (matching the precedent that neither RecoveryLeader nor StagingLiveHitLeader has an arm there); hardcode `->color('success')` in the card's own `toStat()` instead, matching the stub's existing `getRgbColor(): [34, 197, 94]`.

proposed_changes.change: Full rewrite in place: extend ChartWidget, implement DashboardMetricCard, `use BuildsDateFilterChartSeries, RendersDashboardStat, StatHelper` directly (not DashboardWidget). Own mount()/canView()/getCardKey()('unique-scans-leaderboard')/getMaxHeight()/refreshData(). canViewCardData() = the standard COMPANY_METRICS Pro-gate shape (auth()->check() && canView() && (Feature::active(...) || admin_impersonator)). toStat(): headline = the top per-kit count from the current-window rollup (never the kit_id=0 org total -- AC-2), hardcoded ->color('success'), ->chart(chartSeries()). chartSeries() override reads UniqueScanCounts's own buildWidgetCacheKey()-derived monthly cache entries (13 scalar org totals), NOT a new query. leaderboardForSelectedRange()-style method reads ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery::handleRange() via sharedRangeCacheKey() (identical org/start/end/timezone to UniqueScanCounts's call), strips key 0 (the rollup total) from the per-kit ranking, and resolves kit names via a small join/lookup (RecoveryLeaderQuery joins clarity.kits inline; handleRange() returns raw kit_id => count and has NO name, so this card must resolve names itself -- see open question).

questions.q: (a) What data shape does the leaderboard's EXPANDED (detail) view actually need -- a genuine 13-month x per-kit stacked breakdown (like RecoveryLeader's and StagingLiveHitLeader's expanded charts), or just the current-window ranked list (same as the compact card) plus the same org-total-only sparkline? The former requires a new, never-measured ScanPlateStatsBatchQuery shape (handle() deliberately carries no kit dimension -- its docblock: 'the combined 13-month x per-kit rollup was never measured and would take the group count from 13 to roughly 13 x kits against a 2.18B-row table'); the latter is achievable today with zero new queries by reusing handleRange() (ranking) and UniqueScanCounts's cached monthly totals (sparkline).
(b) What does the base-class swap to 'the RecoveryLeader shape' mean precisely, and does it break anything?
questions.answer: RecoveryLeader extends ChartWidget directly and implements DashboardMetricCard, using BuildsDateFilterChartSeries/RendersDashboardStat/StatHelper directly rather than extending the abstract DashboardWidget (which also extends ChartWidget + implements DashboardMetricCard via those same three traits, plus a scalar-per-month getMonthlyData()/getData()/getDescription()/getCardTotal()/getSparklinePoints() that cannot represent a per-kit array). 'Swap the base class' means: own every one of those methods directly, as RecoveryLeader and StagingLiveHitLeader already do. DashboardMetricCard's four required methods (getCardKey, toStat, canViewCardData, lockedStat) are fully satisfiable outside DashboardWidget -- proven by both existing siblings. Side effect discovered and now in scope: DashboardWidget::getStatColor() already carries an arm for 'unique-scans-leaderboard' => 'success' that becomes dead code the moment this swap ships (a ChartWidget-direct card never calls that method), exactly as its own docblock already notes is true for RecoveryLeader's colour. That arm should be removed; the card should hardcode ->color('success') in its own toStat(), matching the KitUsers/RecoveryLeader/StagingLiveHitLeader precedent of hardcoding rather than routing through getStatColor().

questions.q: (c) Does the affiliate_stats_hourly 3.7M-row pre-aggregate (comment 39125) remain a live alternative to the scans_cold GROUP BY, given the 1.56x definitional divergence it flags?
questions.answer: No -- unambiguously settled, on three independent grounds. (1) AffiliateStatsHourly::affiliateStatsQuery() DOES exist and IS live (used by App\Filament\Resources\AffiliateStatsResource.php:126 and App\Filament\Exports\AffiliateStatsExporter.php -- the comment's factual claim was correct; this is a DIFFERENT symbol from the dead AggregateScanCountByHour::affiliateStatsReportQuery() the DEV-2467 reconcile separately ruled out). (2) The canonical KB page okf/models/clickhouse/affiliate_stats_hourly.md states explicitly: 'unique_scans here is NOT period-distinct plates ... Any new surface wanting period-distinct plates must compute uniqExact(ocr) over the window against clarity.scans_cold -- this table cannot answer that question.' (3) DEV-2467's prep-context.json records a direct human product decision, Oscar Nunez, 2026-09-09 (one day AFTER this ticket's 2026-09-08 description rewrite): 'unique by reporting window/timeframe is right' -- settling period-distinct as correct for the entire unique-scans card family this leaderboard belongs to (per the DEV-2409 gate's 2026-08-25 settlement of 'unique = distinct plate (ocr)'). Given the definition is settled as period-distinct and the affiliate table is structurally incapable of answering that question, the comment's cost-driven fork is moot regardless of its cost argument -- reusing it would ship a silently WRONG (1.556x-divergent) number, not merely a cheaper-but-equivalent one. Build against scans_cold as the description instructs.

questions.q: Does handleRange()'s per-kit map need to resolve kit NAMES, and if so, from where? handleRange() returns only kit_id => count; RecoveryLeaderQuery joins clarity.kits FINAL inline for the name, but re-running that join here would be a second, unshared query path.

handleRange()'s docblock records that kit_id CDC-immutability was never measured (unlike ocr's, which DEV-2466 sec 5 confirmed) -- a scan whose kit_id changed mid-window would double-count under both kits in the per-kit map this card displays. Must this ticket validate that assumption (the way sec 5 validated ocr) or apply FINAL to the per-kit read before shipping a customer-visible ranking built on it?
